Livingstone Primary & Nursery School Home
We are a small and friendly one-form entry school in New Barnet set in extensive grounds with spacious classrooms and excellent outdoor facilities on the edge of Hadley Wood.
At Livingstone, we are one big family because although it is a school, it’s also a community where we feel secure, valued and grateful for the time we have or will spend there. We all contribute to this as the teachers are kind and dedicated, planning enjoyable, creative lessons while the children do their best to listen and learn. The minute you step through the doors of the school, you feel loved and in the right place, that is why new students or visitors are warmly welcomed with open arms.
In addition to the friendly ethos, there are many other reasons why Livingstone is so special. The Kingfisher provision (Autism Resource Provision) caters for a range of children with autism providing individual learning programmes in the provision and supporting them in the mainstream classes both with teaching support and by “buddying” them up with other pupils in their year group. Livingstone is also very multicultural and celebrates the ethnic diversity of its pupils. New arrivals, are soon assimilated into their new classes with plenty of friends willing to help them find their feet.
Learning is fun at Livingstone. On Wednesdays, all children experience the “Creative Curriculum” with specialist teachers offering a selection of physical and artistic activities including a range of sports, dance, drama and various arts and crafts. Children have many opportunities to get involved in after-school clubs for football, netball, athletics, yoga and dance. Many pupils also get the chance to represent the school in a variety of competitive sporting events including the Borough Athletics Meeting at Copthall Stadium and Barnet Dance Festival at the Artsdepot. In addition we have a before-school Breakfast Club and after-school Cabin Club to help working families with extra childcare provision.
Both children and staff love working together at Livingstone, it is truly an inclusive school and in the words of one Y6 pupil, “Livingstone is special, it will always welcome you with a smile and a few caring words!”

After School Activity Clubs
We are proud of our commitment to extra-curricular activites and offer our pupils the opportunity to join a variety of clubs throughout the school week catering for different interests.
We have a dedicated team of both teaching staff and external coaches to lead the activities such as:
All Activity Clubs run from the end of the school day at 3.15 until 4.15pm.
Bookings for activity clubs can be made online via school money at the start of every half term. Booking of places are limited and given on a first come first served basis.
Clubs are charged at £4.00 per session, per child and payment must be made for the half term, in advance.
As well as our extra-curricular activities, opportunities are given to groups of children from Years 2 - 6 to extend their learning in our Maths and English Catch-up Clubs. These take place before and after school. Attendance is by invite only and rotated on a termly basis. These are non paying clubs
Should you require any further information regarding our extended hours service please contact Mrs Kelly - Extended Hours Co-ordinator.

Breakfast Club
Livingstone’s Breakfast Club provides a childcare service for parents/carers of pupils from Nursery through to Year 6 attending Livingstone Primary and Nursery School in need of before school care for their children.
Our well established Breakfast Club takes place in ‘The Cabin’ and is managed and staffed by school staff members.
We operate Monday to Friday, term time only (excluding inset days), from 8.00 – 8.45am.
Your child can be dropped off at any time between these times but breakfast is only served until 8.30am.
At 8.45am children will be escorted by staff to their class ready for the school day to begin.
These costs include a healthy breakfast and a range of activities that pupils can access afterwards.
The club is flexible about attendance patterns to accommodate the needs of children and families by offering a book in advance or walk-in service.
Fees for Breakfast Club can be paid by cash or online via School Money or childcare vouchers (please check if the provider is registered with us).

Kingfisher ARP and Mainstream SEND
Practising our big PE skills
Enjoying bikes in our Kingfisher playground
Our Vision
At Livingstone we aim to deliver a high quality education for all our pupils. We have a team which is dedicated to ensuring that pupils with Special Educational Needs and Disability (SEND) receive the very best support to achieve their potential. We have many teachers with specialist skills and experience. All staff keep up to date with current methods of teaching and resources.
We ensure that our mainstream SEND pupils fully participate in all curriculum and extra curriculum of school life.
Kingfisher
At Livingstone we have an additional resourced provision for children with autism called Kingfisher.
Kingfisher includes an assessment provision for pre-school children aged 3 and above, with additional needs which cannot be met within mainstream settings. Our Kingfisher Nursery forms part of Early Years Foundation Stage and provides placements for 12 children.
Our Kingfisher Resourced Provision provides for a small number of children with a diagnosis of Autism from Reception to Year 6. The children have access to a specialist setting with highly qualified and experienced staff. They have access to appropriate mainstream classes in line with their age, individual abilities and needs.
The children have access to a softplay room, sensory room and their own playground all adapted to meet their needs.
Contact our SENCos, Mrs Ferdenzi or Miss Nicholson, through the school office email - office@livingstone.barnetmail.net
The Local Offer
The Local offer gives children and young people with special educational needs, disabilities and their families, information about what support services the local authority expects will be available in their local area.

History
In History, pupils develop their knowledge about Britain’s past and the wider world. It inspires pupils’ curiosity to know about the past and develop skills such as questioning, critical thinking and analysing arguments and evidence. We learn about how different people lived and how different their lives could be, making comparisons with the present. We teach History through an enquiry-led approach encouraging our pupils to be curious, analytic thinkers and learners; it is taught using a subject specific set of skills, knowledge and vocabulary to be built upon each year.
Click here for the National Curriuclum for History:https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/government/uploads/
History at Livingstone
History has been tailored to a ‘Big Question’ which will be answered through specifically planned lessons and ‘Chilli Challenges’. This provides our lessons with a clear focus and depth of study. We identify local links when appropriate and use the ‘Pupil Voice’ to make learning engaging and relevant. Pupils learn through a range of mediums including Literature, Art, Drama, and Multimedia including technology and Music and organised education visits. We have also looked closely at our 'progression of skills' - ensuring that curriculum content is supported by children's developing historical skills across all year groups. The teaching teams have developed 'knowledge organisers' that outline all key learning for each unit of work. Children have access to these to ensure that these key areas of learning are being well covered and understood by the children.

Maths
An exciting measurement lesson
Children using Unifix cubes
Mathematics is a creative and highly interconnected discipline that has been developed over centuries, providing the solution to some of history’s most intriguing problems. It is essential to everyday life, critical to science, technology and engineering, and necessary for financial literacy and most forms of employment.
Click here for the National Curriculum for Mathematics:
https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/national-curriculum-in-england-mathematics-programmes-of-study/national-curriculum-in-england-mathematics-programmes-of-study
Maths at Livingstone
At Livingstone Primary and Nursery school we provide children with a broad and balanced Maths curriculum which encourages curiosity and inspires them through well-adapted maths activities.
The National Curriculum provides the framework for the teaching of Mathematics at Livingstone school. Wherever possible, links will be made to other curriculum areas and computing used to enable pupils to apply and develop their numerical skills.
We follow a curriculum based on the recommendations of the National Centre of Excellence in the Teaching of Mathematics (NCETM) and use the White Rose guidance materials to teach for mastery. This incorporates the following skills: fluency, reasoning and problem solving. These skills are supported using a Concrete, Pictorial, Abstract (CPA) approach.
We regularly use a variety of practical resources and ICT. Some of the children’s favourites include: Numicon, Times Tables Rock Stars, Probots and Beebots.
For a more detailed overview of what topics are taught in each year group please refer to the Curriculum Map in the Curriculum Booklet.
Below are the White Rose Calculation guidance documents. These demonstrate different models, representations and methods that we use in our school to teach Maths.
Curriculum Overview
Times tables Rockstars is an exciting programme we use to practise times tables. It combines the skills of multiplication and division, whilst getting the children to increase in skill and accuracy.
During school, the children complete paper challenges throughout the week and aim to beat their score or time.
Every term, the children take part in 'Battle of the Bands' where they compete to see which class can score the most points. The children enjoy the friendly competition and strive to become the most valuable players.
At home, please encourage your child to use the Rock stars website to play the times tables games. They can earn points to buy new clothes and accessories for their rock star avatar. Also, look out for their name in the Hall of Fame.

Music
Music is a universal language that embodies one of the highest forms of creativity. A high quality music education should engage and inspire pupils to develop a love of music and their talent as musicians, and so increase their self-confidence, creativity and sense of achievement.
Click here for the National Curriculum for Music: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/national-curriculum-in-england-music-programmes-of-study/national-curriculum-in-england-music-programmes-of-study
Music at Livingstone
At Livingstone we enjoy celebrating music together. Our curriculum is designed to provide maximum enjoyment of music, offering a variety of styles of music for children to experience. The children receive music lessons which provide them with an experience of an understanding about the core elements of music: Performing, composing, inter related dimensions of music, listening and the history of music.
During lessons, we allow children the opportunity to express themselves creatively using instruments and composing together. All our compositions are based around a style or piece of music that is listened to and discussed for our own creations. All our lessons include elements of singing, listening and the inter related dimensions of music including understanding music notation, note values and dynamics. We celebrate blues and jazz, hip hop, and a variety of other styles of music.
At Livingstone, we like to celebrate our children’s voices with regular school events. We have weekly singing assemblies for KS1 & KS2 where children learn and rehearse new songs. Annually, Year 2 take part in the Barnet Infant Music Festival, they learn and perform a variety of songs with other schools and perform their own piece either a song or composition.
Our school Choir, that is open to all children from Year 4, also take part each year in the KS2 Barnet Music Festival, learning new songs and performing our own piece. Our school choir meet weekly, and rehearse a variety of fun and challenging music, performing songs at assemblies and school events.
In year 3 the children have weekly lessons learning the recorder with a specialist music teacher from BEATs. This gives them the experience of playing an instruments, playing together as an ensemble and developing and understanding for reading notation. Children are then able to continue with their recorder learning as they progress through KS2.
Livingstone provides individual tuition in different instruments with both private teachers and Barnet Education Arts Trust teachers. We currently offer lessons in keyboard, piano and guitar.

Science
Year 6 dissect lamb hearts
EYFS learn about life cycles of frogs
Year 2 observe how seeds grow in their hydroponics
A high-quality science education provides the foundations for understanding the world through the specific disciplines of biology, chemistry and physics. Science has changed our lives and is vital to the world’s future prosperity, and all pupils should be taught essential aspects of the knowledge, methods, processes and uses of science.
Click here for the National Curriculum for Science: https://www.gov.uk/government/uploads/system/uploads/attachment_data/file/425618/PRIMARY national_curriculum_-_Science.pdf
Science at Livingstone
At Livingstone Primary and Nursery School, Science teaching is based upon the National Curriculum objectives. We provide children with a broad and balanced Science Curriculum which allows children to develop a sound understanding of basic scientific concepts through practical and investigative work. Throughout their Science learning across the school, pupils will be given opportunities to explore the five key enquiry types (Comparative and Fair Testing / Identifying, Classifying and Grouping / Pattern Seeking / Observation Over Time / Research using Secondary Sources). These learning experiences encourage children to develop their key scientific skills (Asking questions / Observing and Measuring / Recording Data / Interpreting and Communicating Results / Making Predictions / Setting up Tests / Evaluating) as well as expanding their knowledge and understanding of scientific vocabulary. Wherever possible, our extensive outside areas are used to develop the children’s understanding of the outside world and for environmental learning.
British Science Week
To ensure that pupils are developing their working scientifically skills we carry out a Science week every year across the school. Pupils from our Early Years classes up to Year 6 all receive the opportunity to explore an investigative question, work with their peers and show case their outcomes to the rest of the school whilst enjoying their science learning. Some recent themes of our Science week have been: Curiosity - What's your question?, Change and Adapt and Time.

Cabin Club
Livingstone’s Cabin Club provides a reliable service for parents/carers in need of after school childcare.
We are committed to providing children with quality play experiences in a relaxed space that is safe and secure and endeavour to create a stimulating environment that will foster their independence and self-esteem.
The club is managed and staffed by school staff members.
We operate from the end of the school day at 3.15 until 5.45pm, Monday to Friday, term time only (excluding inset days).
Children will be collected from class by staff and escorted to ‘The Cabin’ for registration when they can sit and enjoy a light snack too.
During their time at The Cabin Club, children can access a variety of activities that include arts and crafts, computing, board games, reading, writing, small world/role play, construction and outside play.
Children must be registered with The Cabin Club and required sessions must be booked and paid for in advance via School Money or the School Office.

Department for Education
Livingstone are very proud of our results as they are a reflection of the hard work done over many years by pupils and teaching teams. Results change from year to year as they depend on many factors, so we have included information on progress under our assessment results as it shows the positive outcomes for all our pupils.
Click here to access the performance tables page for Livingstone
At Livingstone all of our pupils have regular assessments and we keep detailed records tracking pupil progress and attainment from Nursery to Year 6. All pupils are measured against age specific criteria throughout the year and assessed at:
- working towards the standards (WTS - emerging)
- meeting expected standards (EXS).
- exceeding the standards (GDS - working at Greater Depth).
- below the standard.
Pupils that deemed as Below are assessed on a graded Pre-Key Stage scale.
Year 6 children (Key Stage Two) have to take national SATs tests in English (reading, grammar, punctuation, spelling and maths). The tests are sent to external markers and their scores combined with teacher assessments. Teachers in Year 6 make an assessment of the children’s progress in writing and science. At the end of the year the school receives a combined score for each child which will indicate their attainment in line with national expectations for this year group.

Geography
In Geography, pupils develop their knowledge of different places, people, cultures, natural environments and human settlements. Pupils are encouraged to explore their topics through real-life experience, research and discussion, and through ongoing activities such as map-reading and field work. The children regularly take part in organised educational visits to help develop their geographical understanding of their local area, the UK and the wider world.
Click here for the National Curriculum for Geography: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/national-curriculum-in-england-geography-programmes-of-study
Geography at Livingstone:
In the Early Years Foundation Stage and Year 1, children engage in weekly Forest School activities using our own pond and wildlife area as well as visiting the local parks and woodlands. Year 2 learn all about Transport within our local area; explore the extreme environments of the Polar Regions; and, in summer, enjoy a wonderful day at the seaside learning all about the coastal environment. In Year 3, focus turns to the Hilly and Mountainous areas of the UK and beyond; and this theme extends in Year 4 to the exciting topic of Earthquakes and Volcanoes - always a favourite! In Year 5, children learn all about Rivers and Water Systems and, in Year 6, attention turns to South America and the Rainforest. Geographical skills including map-reading, field work skills and independent research develops as the children progress in their Geographical studies.
Livingstone has been awarded both the Bronze and the Silver 'Primary Geography Quality Mark' through the Geographical Association which demonstrates our commitment to the teaching and learning of Geography across the whole school.

RE
Religious Education helps children explore big questions about life, belief and the world around them. It encourages pupils to think about ideas such as the meaning of life, beliefs about God, right and wrong, and what it means to be human.
Through RE, children develop knowledge and understanding of Christianity, other major religions, and non-religious worldviews, helping them to make sense of the diverse society in which they live.
RE also supports pupils’ personal development and well-being, promoting respect, curiosity and understanding of others.
RE at Livingstone
At Livingstone, we follow the Barnet Agreed Syllabus for Religious Education (2025–2030), which we are currently introducing across the school.
This new approach is built around six “Big Questions” (such as Where do we come from?), helping children to explore beliefs, ideas and values in a structured and meaningful way.
Our RE curriculum supports pupils by:
Children learn about a range of religions and worldviews, including Christianity, Judaism, Islam, Hinduism and Humanism, reflecting both the national and local community.
Lessons are designed to be engaging and thought-provoking, using discussion, stories, artefacts and creative activities to deepen understanding.
A developing curriculum
We are currently rolling out the new Barnet syllabus in stages, ensuring that teaching is carefully planned and builds progressively across year groups.
This approach ensures that children revisit key ideas over time, developing a deeper understanding as they move through the school.
Guidance
For further information about RE in schools, please visit: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/religious-education-guidance-in-english-schools-non-statutory-guidance-2010
For a more detailed overview of what topics are taught in each year group please refer to the Curriculum Map in the Curriculum Booklet.

Livingstone Toddler Group
Tuesdays 9:30 am – 11:30 am
We have a well-established parent and toddler group running since 2008 who welcome all parents and carers with children under the age of five.
We have a wide variety of clean toys and fun activities suitable for all children of pre-school age, as well as a small outside area.
During the sessions, the children are offered healthy snacks and they are encouraged to sit at tables. There is unlimited tea and coffee for all important parents and carers.
Livingstone Toddler group provides a safe, fun and friendly atmosphere. Both parents / carers and children have the opportunity to meet new friends and to interact with each other.
Forest Toddler Group
On a Thursday between 9am and 11am, we open our Pond Area to children 3 or under. It is £2 per child.
